name: Hunched eagle marker
slug: High-ranking hunched eagle Elrus calls a hobgoblin legion standard.
description: A high-ranking hunched eagle on a decorative base, separate from the poker-chip troop tokens. Elrus calls it a hobgoblin legion standard.

log.summary: Vecna was tapping this piece and left it on the table. Walker, still holding it, pocketed it and later set it on Elrus's square table. Elrus says it has nothing to do with a mountain or a waterfall. Walker guesses it might be a tuning fork. In a recalled scene, Grixto pulls a different hunched eagle from a table and leaves once the plan is sorted.
notes: The high-ranking piece Vecna was tapping: a hunched eagle on a decorative base, not one of the poker-chip tokens. He left it on the table. Walker was still holding it, pocketed it, and later set it on Elrus's square table.

Elrus calls it a hobgoblin legion standard and says it has nothing to do with a mountain or a waterfall. Walker guesses it might be a tuning fork. In a recalled scene, Grixto pulls a different hunched eagle from a table and leaves once the plan is sorted.

log.summary: Walker calls the marker the golden eagle. Vecna was tapping it on a table before Walker produced it; Walker had taken the tapping for boredom and now reads it as a hint. Placed on the war-table map, the piece lights the map, and Walker thinks the party must find that table or use this object on it. He believes the eagle is only half of a pair, with the counterpart at Vecna's former palace in Nyx, the headquarters with the big red wall. Dana distinguishes it from the helm: Walker has not had the eagle the whole time, while he has worn the helm continuously.
notes: Walker calls it the golden eagle. Vecna was tapping it on a table before Walker produced it. Walker thought Vecna was bored and now reads the tapping as a hint.

Dana distinguishes it from the helm: Walker has not had the eagle the whole time, while he has been wearing the helm continuously.

log.summary: The hunched eagle marker is now understood to be a troop marker or troop identifier rather than a chess piece. Walker brought it back from Grixto's hideout and currently holds it. The party tested it in the Soul identifier, and it came back clean, showing no phylactery or soul fragment, so it has been crossed off the list.
notes: A troop marker or troop identifier rather than a chess piece, brought back by Walker from Grixto's hideout. Walker holds it.
